papers.title: JoyAI-Video-Edit: Real-Time Open-Ended Video Editing with Autoregressive Diffusion

summary.tldr: JoyAI-Video-Edit is a 16B-parameter autoregressive diffusion framework that enables real-time, open-ended 720p video editing at 30 FPS on a single Nvidia B200 GPU without future frame access.
key_points: Utilizes a 16B-parameter autoregressive diffusion model designed for real-time video editing without predefined clip durations.
Combines Source-Anchored Distribution Matching Distillation (SA-DMD) with chunk-wise autoregressive adaptation to maintain source fidelity in two-step generation.
Employs Long-Horizon Autoregressive Distillation to reduce train-inference mismatch and mitigate long-term accumulated temporal drift.
Achieves streaming 720p performance at ~30 FPS on a single Nvidia B200 GPU.
summary.why_it_matters: It proves that open-ended, streaming video editing can achieve real-time 30 FPS performance while maintaining temporal consistency and matching offline editor quality.

papers.title: MerchantBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Long-Term Coherence in E-Commerce Operations

summary.tldr: MerchantBench is a 365-day e-commerce simulation benchmark using 98,843 real product records and 26 tools to test LLM agents' long-term coherence across extended operational horizons.
key_points: Evaluates agents across four e-commerce domains: Product Sourcing, Listing/Pricing Control, Cash-Flow Management, and Mixed-Latency Feedback Adaptation.
Couples fast Upstream Supplier Events with delayed Downstream Order Outcomes, forcing agents to track multi-step order lifecycles and adapt past decisions.
Tested eight LLMs across two agent frameworks over 48 full 365-day simulated runs.
The top-performing LLM setup achieved only 27.3% of the mean final net assets earned by human participants.
summary.why_it_matters: The benchmark exposes a severe performance gap in current LLMs when forced to maintain coherent, multi-step decisions over long timeframes with delayed real-world feedback.

papers.title: InfiniSplat: Implicit Gaussian Decoding for Large-Baseline Monocular View Synthesis

summary.tldr: InfiniSplat introduces a feed-forward single-image 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that uses geometry-guided sampling and an implicit decoder to replace pixel-aligned primitives with surface-aligned representations for large-baseline view synthesis.
key_points: Transitions from fixed, pixel-aligned image-grid representations to surface-aligned 3D Gaussian layouts.
Uses geometry-guided sampling to position 2D supports based on depth-induced local surface structures.
Employs a query-conditioned implicit decoder to predict Gaussian attributes from image features sampled at the support locations.
Demonstrates zero-shot generalization from Hypersim synthetic indoor training data to complex open-world environments.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables accurate, structurally coherent novel view synthesis from a single image across large viewpoint shifts without requiring per-scene optimization or multi-view capture.

papers.title: AURORA-LM: Autoencoding Unified Representation for Continuous-Latent Diffusion Language Modeling

summary.tldr: AURORA-LM introduces a continuous-latent diffusion language model combining a Query-based Encoder-Decoder for prefix-aligned text latents with a Block-causal Diffusion Transformer using flow matching.
key_points: Separates high-capacity decodable latent construction from generative distribution modeling.
Uses a Query-based Encoder-Decoder to form prefix-aligned latent sequences and a Block-causal Diffusion Transformer for left-to-right block generation with parallel intra-block denoising.
Restricts the noisy-input pathway while preserving full clean-latent targets, scales noise-level distribution to latent width, and employs self-trajectory consistency.
Outperforms evaluated continuous and diffusion language models on OpenWebText generation and XSum summarization, scaling to 1B parameters using 1500 EFLOPs on Ascend NPUs.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that continuous-latent diffusion models can achieve superior text generation and summarization performance without sacrificing token-level decoder capacity.

papers.title: Hunyuan3D-Buffalo 1.0: A Unified Multimodal Model for Scalable 3D Generation, Understanding, and Editing

summary.tldr: Hunyuan3D-Buffalo 1.0 is a unified 3D multimodal framework that integrates 3D understanding, text-to-3D generation, instruction-guided editing, and text-grounded part generation within a single architecture.
key_points: Trained on a 87M-scale 3D multimodal corpus containing 25M understanding samples, 50M text-to-3D pairs, and 12M editing pairs generated via Nano3D-v2.
Combines Hunyuan3D-VLM for semantic, structural, and spatial understanding with Hunyuan3D DiT for high-fidelity 3D synthesis.

Leverages Hunyuan3D-VLM to supply multimodal semantic conditions for generation while conditioning diffusion on source object representations during editing and part generation to preserve unedited regions.
Demonstrates through empirical analysis that joint training on generation and understanding directly enhances 3D editing performance.
summary.why_it_matters: It proves that unified multimodal pre-training across understanding and generation solves data scarcity in 3D editing and improves overall geometric consistency.

papers.title: Knowledge-Geometry Decoupling: Refreshable Pretrained Transfer for Streaming Recommendation

summary.tldr: KGD decouples pretrained behavioral knowledge from task-specific geometry using Behavioral Multi-Token Prediction and Anchored Calibration Residuals, enabling continuous model refreshing without task-gradient interference in streaming recommendation.
key_points: Behavioral Multi-Token Prediction (BMTP) replaces next-token prediction by selecting only semantically or collaboratively related future items as supervision to eliminate spurious transitions.
Knowledge-Geometry Decoupling (KGD) separates parameters into a refreshable encoder and a task learner that accesses encoder states via read-only cross-attention.
Task-specific geometry is written using Anchored Calibration Residual (ACR), which operates orthogonal to pretrained embeddings to preserve downstream adaptations during updates.
Demonstrates a 4-12% improvement across eight public benchmarks and sustained performance over a 90-day production stream where standard baselines stall.
In a live Shopee Homepage Search A/B test, KGD achieved a 1.75% increase in GMV per user and a 1.53% increase in advertising revenue.
summary.why_it_matters: It solves parameter conflict during continual pretrain-transfer refreshes, allowing industrial recommendation systems to update behavioral models in production without disrupting task-specific adaptations.

papers.title: PCSD: Persistent Consistency for Self-Distillation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: PCSD improves agentic reinforcement learning by deriving continuous token-level self-distillation weights from the local persistence of teacher-favoring signals using adaptive windows, exponential decay, and trend-aware modulation.
key_points: PCSD addresses sparse RL rewards by combining dense teacher guidance with sparse outcome feedback via joint optimization with GRPO.
Token-level distillation weights are computed using adaptive windows and exponentially decayed aggregation to measure persistent relative teacher support.
Trend-aware modulation attenuates locally declining teacher support, and sigmoid gating outputs continuous weights.
Evaluated on ALFWorld, PCSD outperformed GRPO by up to 15.6 points and SDAR by up to 6.2 points, while gaining 15.8 points over GRPO on unseen splits without inference-time skills.
summary.why_it_matters: PCSD provides robust, dense token-level supervision in multi-turn RL environments, mitigating teacher noise and improving agent generalization on unseen tasks.

papers.title: Quo Vadis, World Modeling?

summary.tldr: This paper introduces Agent-Centric Interactive World Proxies, shifting world modeling from raw physical-state prediction to agent-usable information transitions like execution outcomes, memory retrieval, and verification signals.
key_points: Formalizes six functional forms of world proxies: dynamics, spatial, execution, memory/experience, skill, and reward/verification proxies.

Categorizes proxy impact across three agent levels: L.1 Inference-Time Guidance (in-context decision enrichment), L.2 Training-Time Optimization (synthetic rollouts and rewards), and L.3 Agent-Proxy Co-Evolution (continuous joint updating via real-world evidence).
Redefines world modeling feedback from narrow state transitions to broader actionable information required for agent self-improvement.
summary.why_it_matters: It expands world modeling beyond physical simulation, offering a structured framework to safely and efficiently train and guide AI agents using controllable, low-cost feedback.

papers.title: PAST-Bench: Benchmarking the Foundations of Recursive Self-Improvement in Personal Agents

summary.tldr: PAST-Bench benchmarks recursive self-improvement in personal AI agents across controlled task sequences, evaluating performance gains from retained experience against Hermes+, an agent framework with five targeted interventions across the agent loop.
key_points: PAST-Bench evaluates 7 base models and 4 agent frameworks over 26 scenarios and 204 episodes across memory, procedural reuse, information gathering, and state update.
The benchmark uses ordered task sequences in fresh sessions with retained experience toggled on and off to verify if performance gains follow intended save, retrieve, and update pathways.
Hermes+ introduces five targeted interventions to the Hermes agent loop, increasing average gains from retained experience and showing its highest improvement on replacing outdated state.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a standardized diagnostic framework to measure whether and how persistent personal agents convert historical session experience into genuine, pathway-verified self-improvement.

papers.title: To Add Is Machine, To Delete Is Human: Measuring and Mitigating Deletion Avoidance in LLM Code Editing

summary.tldr: Researchers identify deletion avoidance in LLMs, showing models fail to remove unnecessary code, and demonstrate that post-training targeting deletion reduces this behavior and improves overall code editing.
key_points: Frontier models reach at most 71.7% deletion recall on solved SWE-bench Verified tasks, frequently using a 'Guard-and-Go' pattern that wraps target code instead of deleting it in 29.0% of passing patches.
Retrofitting 34 SWE-bench Verified tasks with tests requiring code removal dropped four frontier models' pass rates from 63.2% to 41.9%.
On CanItDelete, a new 200-task pure-deletion benchmark, top models failed 20% of tasks, while smaller open models dropped to an 18.0% success rate.
Prompting GPT-5.6 Sol with exact target lines reduced incomplete deletions but capped success at 80.5% due to over-deletion or unexpected additions.
summary.why_it_matters: LLM code editors generate test-passing patches that systematically bloat codebases and increase technical debt by retaining code meant for removal.

papers.title: Video-DeepResearch: Towards the Next-Generation Multimodal Deepresearch Agent

summary.tldr: Video-DeepResearch extends multimodal agents to continuous video via a decoupled perception-exploration pipeline, stage-wise tool unlocking, and GRPO reinforcement learning, outperforming proprietary models on complex video reasoning.
key_points: Identifies modality bias (preferring text search over visual tools) and parametric knowledge leakage (relying on memory over tool execution) as key agent failure modes.
Uses a two-stage training paradigm combining supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to enable autonomous web and visual exploration.
Implements a decoupled perception-exploration architecture with stage-wise tool unlocking to enforce dense visual grounding before executing web retrieval.
Introduces Video-DR-Bench, a benchmark containing 200 complex multi-hop visual question answering instances.
Video-DeepResearch-35B-A3B achieves a state-of-the-art 64.0% accuracy on Video-DR-Bench, surpassing Claude-4.5-Sonnet (59.0%), Gemini 2.5 Pro (57.5%), and GPT-5 (52.5%).
summary.why_it_matters: The framework demonstrates that open-weights models trained with stage-wise tool policies and RL can outperform leading proprietary LLMs on complex, multi-hop video research tasks.

papers.title: Any-OPD: Heterogeneous On-Policy Distillation for Flow-Matching Models via Representation-Space Bridging

summary.tldr: Any-OPD enables on-policy distillation between heterogeneous latent flow-matching models by comparing decoded outputs within a frozen, model-agnostic vision representation space rather than relying on matching architectures, VAE latents, or timestep grids.
key_points: Bypasses latent coordinate mismatches by treating the teacher as a black-box sampler and comparing decoded outputs in a model-agnostic vision representation space.
Establishes trajectory alignment across mismatched schedules by matching continuous noise levels instead of discrete step indices.
Uses a brief anchoring phase where teacher samples are re-encoded through the student's VAE to prevent domain mismatch during on-policy gradient calculation.
Distilling the 12B FLUX.1-dev into the 2.5B SD3.5-Medium raised PickScore from 0.846 to 0.884 and HPSv3 from 9.12 to 10.97, whereas direct latent regression failed to train.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows developers to distill state-of-the-art generative capabilities from large, proprietary-style teacher models into much smaller deployment models even when their latent spaces, VAEs, and architectures are completely incompatible.

papers.title: OmniPack: Unified Token Compression for Efficient Omni-modal Large Language Models

summary.tldr: OmniPack is a training-free framework that combines pre-LLM structural token compression with inner-LLM query-conditioned semantic refinement to optimize efficiency in omni-modal large language models.
key_points: Coordinates pre-LLM structural compression using modality-specific importance, global coverage, and similarity-aware merging.
Performs inner-LLM semantic refinement using textual guidance and audio-visual collaboration to consolidate task-relevant representations.
Preserves 98.0% of full performance on Qwen2.5-Omni-7B while reducing computational FLOPs to 16.7%.
Retains 92.9% of baseline performance when compressing FLOPs down to 6.8% on Qwen2.5-Omni-7B.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables drastically reduced computational overhead for audio-visual LLM inference without requiring retrained models or sacrificing significant task performance.

papers.title: UniWorld-Design: From Pixel Generation to Layer-Native Design

summary.tldr: UniWorld-Design introduces a layer-native framework featuring Text-to-RGBA and Image-to-Layer models that generate, decompose, and edit images as complete semantic RGBA layers rather than flat pixel grids.
key_points: Text-to-RGBA (T2RGBA) generates standalone RGBA assets directly from text prompts, outperforming LayerDiffuse and OmniAlpha on CLIP Score.

Image-to-Layer (I2L) uses a finished image, global instructions, and per-layer prompts to jointly output ordered, complete semantic RGBA layers representing whole objects rather than visible-pixel partitions.
I2L's instruction interface enables agentic operations including top-level decomposition, recursive decomposition, and targeted extraction.
On the Crello benchmark, I2L reduces per-layer RGB L1 error by 37% and increases Alpha Soft IoU by 34% compared to Qwen-Image-Layered.
summary.why_it_matters: By treating complete RGBA layers as atomic units, generative models enable realistic, flexible image editing where individual elements can be moved or removed without leaving pixel artifacts.

papers.title: CAPEval: A Decoupled Caption Evaluation across Understanding and Generation

summary.tldr: CAPEval decouples caption quality into Coverage and Precision, revealing that Coverage correlates with downstream multimodal understanding performance while Precision predicts text-to-image generation performance.
key_points: CAPEval uses human-written ground-truth captions and human-verified atomic checklist items to decouple quality metrics.
Coverage measures how thoroughly a caption captures ground-truth factual content.
Precision measures the factual correctness rate of the claims expressed within a caption.
Controlled end-to-end experiments across 10 captioners and 4 model families showed a task-dependent dissociation where Coverage drives understanding and Precision drives generation.
summary.why_it_matters: Decoupling caption metrics allows researchers to select and optimize captioners specifically tailored for either multimodal understanding or text-to-image generation tasks.

papers.title: TurnSight: Turn-Level Hindsight Self-Distillation for Tool-Integrated Reasoning

summary.tldr: TurnSight is a turn-level hindsight self-distillation framework for tool-integrated reasoning that derives dense supervision from execution-conditioned hindsight and cross-horizon agreement to adaptively modulate RL advantages.
key_points: Addresses credit assignment limitations in trajectory-level RL and token-level self-distillation by operating directly on the turn-level structure of tool interactions.
Derives teacher supervision from execution-conditioned hindsight states actually visited by the agent, rather than ground-truth answers or retrieved skills.
Constructs multiple hindsight views across different lookahead horizons and selects reliable signals using cross-horizon directional agreement.
Normalizes the selected hindsight signals across sibling rollouts to adaptively modulate RL advantages while preserving the original optimization direction.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves reinforcement learning for long-horizon tool-integrated LLMs by offering fine-grained, state-grounded credit assignment without relying on external privileged context.

papers.title: Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning LLMs: Inference Regimes, Evaluation, and Reproducibility

summary.tldr: This paper establishes a unified three-axis framework for test-time scaling in LLMs, standardizing inference regimes, evaluation profiles, and reproducibility requirements while releasing over 2 billion full reasoning traces.
key_points: Formalizes test-time scaling as budgeted inference over an autoregressive prefix tree across three regimes: single-trajectory sequential, leaf-level with terminal reduction, and prefix-level scaling.
Introduces an evaluation profile and diagnostic metrics that separate end-to-end system performance from candidate-bank diagnostics while bounding repeated-sampling metrics.
Defines reproducibility requirements by distinguishing exact replay from distributional reproducibility and detailing the necessary artifacts for both.
Organizes the open-weight reasoning ecosystem and releases a dataset of over 2 billion full reasoning traces containing verifier and token-level signals.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes standardized accounting for compute, protocols, and evaluation, enabling rigorous, reproducible comparisons across disparate inference-time search and sampling strategies.

papers.title: ReflectRL: Learning from Golden Negative Trajectories via Reflective-to-Direct Reasoning

summary.tldr: ReflectRL is a lightweight plug-and-play framework that uses failed expert trajectories (Golden Negative Trajectories) during on-policy training to elicit reflective reasoning and transfer it back to direct reasoning.
key_points: Identifies the Reflection Advantage: reflecting on a flawed trajectory for hard problems is more effective than solving them directly from scratch.
Introduces Reflective Reasoning using Golden Negative Trajectories that are usually discarded in trajectory-guided methods when expert models fail.
Employs a Reflective-to-Direct Policy Transition to transfer acquired reflective reasoning capabilities back into direct reasoning capabilities.
Evaluated across 9 benchmarks, 4 LLM backbones, and 4 on-policy training methods with minimal overhead.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables LLMs to convert previously wasted expert failure data into effective training signals without requiring successful reference trajectories.

papers.title: Interpretable Adaptive Sampling for LLM Test-Time Scaling

summary.tldr: A lightweight fuzzy controller dynamically assigns LLM test-time sampling budgets per query based on prompt complexity and model confidence, reducing average samples while maintaining reasoning performance.
key_points: Replaces fixed per-query test-time scaling budgets with dynamic allocation using an interpretable fuzzy controller.
Controller uses prompt complexity and model confidence signals to assign fewer samples to easy prompts and more to hard prompts.
Evaluated under a fair-alignment protocol with matched decoding settings and controlled answer selection on QA and math reasoning tasks.
Outperforms best-of-N, compute-aware scaling, and self-certainty baselines while performing near selector-matched full-budget controls with fewer samples.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables more compute-efficient LLM inference by providing inspectable, query-specific sample allocation without sacrificing output accuracy.

papers.title: Logic Before Language: Pre-pretraining on Formal Derivations Fosters Skill Acquisition and Compressibility

summary.tldr: Logic pre-pretraining (Logic-PPT) initializes language models on formal derivations, accelerating natural language skill acquisition and improving model compressibility at scale.
key_points: Evaluated at a 100B-token scale, Logic-PPT achieves 80% accuracy on linguistic tasks using 36 billion fewer tokens than standard initialization.
Formal derivations train models to bind variables, connect quantifiers and relational dependencies, and compose predicate-argument structures over long contexts.
Mechanistically, Logic-PPT induces a lower-rank, spectrally concentrated representation space that persists through training.
The resulting representation space improves post-training pruning, enabling a pruned model to match dense baseline performance at approximately 33% sparsity.
summary.why_it_matters: Using formal logic as a pre-training phase significantly reduces the token budget required to achieve target task accuracy and yields smaller, highly compressible models.

papers.title: Risky Business: Measuring The Faithfulness-Safety Tension

summary.tldr: Researchers identify a fundamental alignment tension between reasoning faithfulness and safety in Large Reasoning Models, introducing the HazMart benchmark and a Targeted Reasoning Replacement technique to measure and steer these behavior trade-offs.
key_points: Targeted Reasoning Replacement (TRR) directly intervenes in Chain-of-Thought traces to substitute unsafe or illogical thoughts, evaluating whether models adopt or reject unsafe reasoning.
Benchmarking reveals contrasting tradeoffs: DeepSeek-R1-Llama-70B shows 97.5% faithfulness but only 12.3% safety, whereas QwQ-32B achieves 73.9% safety but drops to 74.7% faithfulness.
Mechanistic analysis of QwQ-32B shows that faithfulness and safety correspond to anti-correlated internal representation directions that peak at the action-commit token.
Representation steering targeting the safety direction increases QwQ-32B safe behavior by 9 percentage points without degrading base capabilities.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding and resolving the tension between faithfulness and safety is critical for building trustworthy, monitorable AI systems that predictably reject unsafe actions.

papers.title: Muon Meets Mamba: Spectral Optimization for State Space Models

summary.tldr: Applying the Muon optimizer specifically to the output projection of Mamba-2 130M improves token efficiency over AdamW, whereas applying it to input projections or both projections yields worse results.
key_points: Evaluation conducted on Mamba-2 130M comparing Muon (which uses Newton-Schulz iterations for spectral norm steepest descent) against AdamW.
Muon's performance gains are localized: applying it solely to the output projection outperforms training the input projection or both projections combined.
The efficiency gains hold across two corpora, two token budgets, and overtrained regimes past the compute-optimal point.
Conditioning improvements do not drive the performance gains; while Muon lowers condition numbers for both projections, the input projection does not benefit performance.
summary.why_it_matters: Selective application of spectral optimizers like Muon to specific layers enables token-efficiency gains in non-Transformer architectures like State Space Models.

papers.title: Sparse Weight Decomposition for Efficient Circuit Extraction

summary.tldr: Sparse Weight Decomposition (SWD) reparameterizes pretrained linear transformer weight matrices into two sparse factors, creating addressable circuit units for extraction without training auxiliary sparse models or incurring high computational costs.
key_points: Factorizes each linear weight matrix into two sparse factors connected by shared intermediate coordinates that act as circuit units.
Matches the held-out fidelity of baselines like Transcoder using under 1% of the training data, and offers a zero-data variant for per-step analysis.
Achieves equivalent circuit sufficiency and necessity targets with fewer selected units and active read/write edges across GPT-2, Qwen2.5, and Qwen3.5-27B.
Supports full-model replacement across all attention and MLP weight matrices via fine-tuning of non-zero factor values.
summary.why_it_matters: SWD significantly reduces the computational burden and data requirements for mechanistically interpreting LLMs without sacrificing fidelity or introducing a gap between analyzed features and original weights.

papers.title: Cross-Model KV Cache Transfer in LLM Families: A Closed-Form Linear Mapping for Prefill Reuse

summary.tldr: A closed-form ridge regression mapper enables cross-model KV cache transfer between different-sized LLM family members, bypassing prefill computation by mapping source KV pairs to target layers.
key_points: Linear structure exists across matched-KV pairs: multi-layer source inputs explain up to 79% key and 65% value variance on Qwen3 14B->32B.
Mapper pipeline strips RoPE for position-free fitting, selects top-k predictive source layers per target layer, and uses ridge regression trained on 500 FineWeb-Edu sequences.
Linear mapping preserves 73-98% receiver accuracy on four of six model pairs, while a non-linear MLP recovers up to +37 percentage points HellaSwag retention on failure cases.
Transfer achieves 2.7-25x speedup compared to re-prefilling and maintains stability over multi-turn handoffs.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly reduces compute latency and cost when dynamically routing or swapping context between different-sized models within the same family.

papers.title: Omega-S: A Functional Resilience Index for LLM Fine-Tuning

summary.tldr: Omega-S is a data-free, weight-only penalty that reduces catastrophic forgetting in LLM fine-tuning by regularizing node degree variance, adding under 4% step overhead without requiring old data or Fisher matrices.
key_points: Requires no prior task data, Fisher matrices, or saved initial weights, adding <4% computational overhead per step.
Improves Llama-3-8B HumanEval pass@1 retention ratio from 62.9% to 84.1% (0.173 to 0.238 absolute) when fine-tuning LoRA from code to prose.
Outperforms standard weight decay on 10/10 seeds (p=0.002) and Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC) on 8/10 seeds (p=0.014).
Empirical gradient analysis shows the topological Tr(A^3) objective acts primarily as a penalty on node degree variance (row magnitude in square modules, directional alignment in non-square modules).
Identifies a high baseline variance in low-rank fine-tuning: identical configurations across identical hardware yield a 0.104 standard deviation in retention ratio.
summary.why_it_matters: Omega-S offers an easily implemented three-line training loss addition that significantly preserves base model capabilities during targeted fine-tuning without the memory and data overhead of traditional regularization methods.

security.title: When Agents Learn to Be You: Benchmarking Privacy Leakage, Impersonation Risk, and Defenses in Persona Skills

summary.tldr: AntiSkillBench is a new benchmark designed to systematically evaluate skill-level privacy leakage, attribute disclosure, behavioral impersonation, and existing defense mechanisms across persona-skill pipelines in downstream agents.
key_points: AntiSkillBench includes 7,500 persona-grounded dialogue traces derived from 50 detailed profiles across various task scenarios.
Evaluates three skill-distillation strategies for privacy and impersonation risks, spanning explicit attributes, communication styles, and personality traits.
Tests four defense configurations incorporating online/post-hoc interventions, active risk suppression, and passive provenance protection.
Empirical evaluations on three frontier agents reveal that risks persist across model backbones, and existing defenses fail to generalize across distillation protocols.
summary.why_it_matters: Persona skills concentrate personal interaction history into reusable agent artifacts, creating persistent privacy and impersonation vulnerabilities that current defenses cannot reliably mitigate.

security.title: Empirical Analysis of Evasion and Poisoning Against Malware Data Drift Detection

summary.tldr: This empirical study analyzes how evasion and poisoning attacks affect machine learning-based malware classifiers and data drift detectors when used in combination.
key_points: Evaluates the joint impact of evasion and poisoning attacks on both malware classifiers and integrated data drift detection tools.
Identifies that the distinct structural and functional characteristics of data drift detectors cause adversarial attacks to behave differently than they do against standalone classifiers.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding how adversarial attacks bypass or manipulate data drift detectors is critical for securing machine learning-based malware detection pipelines against long-term operational threats.

security.title: A Security-Oriented Lifecycle Model for Large Language Model Systems

summary.tldr: A new security-oriented LLM lifecycle model organizes systems around security boundaries via 32 pipeline stages, a 12-stage LLMOps pillar, and a 9-category governance pillar to address regulatory visibility gaps in development.
key_points: Organizes the LLM pipeline into four core layers (Data, Model, Distribution, Application) spanning 32 stages, featuring 13 newly introduced stages that isolate distinct security concerns.

Supported by a 12-stage LLMOps pillar and a 9-category governance pillar covering explicit security activities like data provenance verification, artifact signing, agentic permission control, and decommissioning.

Governance mapping against NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act, and ISO/IEC 42001 demonstrates that regulatory evidence clusters around deployment stages, leaving critical early development stages (data selection, alignment, capability boundaries) with minimal regulatory visibility.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a structured lifecycle framework to identify and mitigate security risks during early development stages before systems reach deployment.

security.title: DiagChain: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Agents on Evidence-Grounded Attack Chain Reconstruction

summary.tldr: DiagChain is a diagnostic benchmark featuring the MAIN-69 scenario suite and five stage-wise metrics to evaluate LLM agents on evidence-grounded attack chain reconstruction.
key_points: MAIN-69 consists of 69 scenarios comprising 849 reference steps across multiple operating systems, evidence noise levels, and chain lengths.
Introduces Evidence-Centric Retrieval-Augmented Generation (ECRAG), which pairs evidence retrieval with an evolving structured representation of the attack chain.
Establishes five complementary metrics designed to isolate intermediate reasoning errors and evaluate distinct reconstruction stages.
Evaluations of six LLMs showed the top-performing configuration achieved only a 39.6% step-level success rate.
Error analysis indicates smaller models fail at integrating retrieved evidence into outputs, while larger models struggle primarily with chronological ordering of evidence.
summary.why_it_matters: Stage-wise diagnostic evaluation exposes specific reasoning and ordering bottlenecks in cybersecurity LLM agents that aggregate end-to-end accuracy metrics obscure.

security.title: AI Forensics Across White-, Grey-, and Black-Box Access: A Process Model and Research Agenda for Post-Incident Investigation of AI Systems

summary.tldr: A new AI forensics framework introduces a four-phase process model matrix and an order of volatility structured around white-, grey-, and black-box investigator access levels.
key_points: Defines a four-phase process model matrix covering collection, preservation, analysis, and reporting mapped against three access levels (white-, grey-, and black-box).
Establishes an AI-specific order of volatility spanning runtime state, context windows, logs, retrieval stores, model artifacts, and training lineage.

Identifies critical open research problems including black-box preservation, model version attestation, uncertainty quantification for surrogate-based analysis, and chain of custody for mutable AI artifacts.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a structured methodology for post-incident investigations, enabling practitioners to properly collect and analyze AI artifacts based on their level of system access.

security.title: SkillJack: Persistent Skill Backdoors in Self-Evolving Agents

summary.tldr: SkillJack is the first attack targeting the experience-to-skill pipeline of self-evolving agents, embedding persistent malicious behaviors into an agent's reusable skill repertoire via its own learning process.
key_points: SkillJack operates via sanitization whitewashing, cross-layer promotion, and persistence isolation to bypass contextual retrieval defenses.
Evaluated on SkillX and Anything2Skill using 150 trajectories across four policy-risk categories, safety detection dropped from 98.5% on raw poisoned trajectories to 11.4% on extracted skills.
Achieved attack success rates of 56.2% on SkillX and 89.2% on Anything2Skill.
80.0% of skill-mediated attacks remained active after the original poisoned source records were deleted, with some skills unintentionally triggering on benign queries.
summary.why_it_matters: Self-evolving agents can permanently internalize backdoors into their skill libraries, rendering memory deletion and context-level guardrails ineffective against hidden exploits.

security.title: SkillSentry: Adaptive Honey Worlds for Dynamic Safety Testing of Agent Skills

summary.tldr: SkillSentry is a dynamic safety-testing framework that uses LLM-simulated environments with adaptive honey worlds and decoy resources to detect conditional malware in LLM agent skills.
key_points: Infers intended skill boundaries and builds LLM-simulated honey worlds containing controlled decoy resources to trigger environment-dependent malicious behaviors.
Adaptively generates task trajectories to explore state space, comparing skill-enabled runs with matched no-skill executions.
Grounds identified suspicious actions directly in source code and verified execution traces before finalizing safety decisions.
Outperforms standard scanners on benchmarks with 99.50% Recall and 96.26% average F1 score.
Maintains an average F1 score of 92.95% under semantics-preserving evasion attacks, compared to 80.07% for top baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables robust detection of complex, state-dependent agent skill vulnerabilities that bypass traditional static code analysis and one-shot evaluation methods.

security.title: Attacking and Defending Multi-Agent Collaborative Filtering Systems Through Connectivity

summary.tldr: Researchers adapted multi-agent system attacks and defenses to LLM-powered collaborative filtering, demonstrating how candidate count and catalog concentration connectivity impact system vulnerability.
key_points: Evaluates security under two connectivity axes using the AgentCF framework: user-side interaction density (candidate count) and item catalog overlap across users (catalog concentration).
Adapts multi-agent system (MAS) attacks and defenses to LLM recommendation pipelines, confirming partial transferability of previous MAS findings.
Identifies role asymmetries between user and item agents, non-monotonic temporal dynamics in attack efficacy, and divergent patterns between dissemination and extraction attack goals.
Explores epidemic-inspired static metrics to rank collaborative filtering configurations by expected attack outcomes for low-cost robustness assessments.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding how network connectivity influences attack dissemination enables developers to design more resilient multi-agent LLM recommendation architectures.

security.title: Attribute-based Undetectable Watermarking for Generative AI Models

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced the first attribute-based undetectable watermarking scheme for generative AI, enabling fine-grained, policy-controlled detection to prevent watermark sanitization, scope abuse, and user profiling.
key_points: Constrains detection keys using specific attribute policies so a key only identifies outputs meeting its designated criteria while leaving outside outputs computationally indistinguishable.
Integrates constrained pseudorandom functions (CPRFs), pseudorandom error-correcting codes, and randomness recovery procedures directly into generative models.
Formalizes security properties including consistency, adaptive robustness to bounded corruptions, undetectability, and soundness under standard cryptographic assumptions.
Demonstrates practical feasibility and effectiveness through a working prototype and empirical evaluation.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows AI developers to safely delegate detection capabilities to third parties without risking watermark removal or unauthorized tracking of non-targeted outputs.

security.title: Test-time reasoning effort and unauthorized tool use in language-model agents: a prespecified equivalence study

summary.tldr: A prespecified study on GPT-5.6 using the TRIO-20 benchmark found that increasing test-time reasoning effort from low to max produced zero unauthorized tool calls and did not increase authorization violations.
key_points: Evaluated GPT-5.6 across 14 confirmatory scenarios in TRIO-20 (840 total trajectories across Terra and Sol tiers) under low and max reasoning effort.
Zero unauthorized tool calls were observed, placing exact one-sided 95% upper limit violation rates below 3.50% for Terra and 5.21% for Sol.
The interaction effect of reasoning effort on violation rates fell within the prespecified equivalence margin of ±7.01 percentage points on Terra (interval of ±4.34 percentage points).
Higher reasoning effort increased rule-probe inspection rates across all conditions, notably where probing had no instrumental payoff (-14.3 points, 95% CI -27.4 to +1.2).
summary.why_it_matters: Operators can scale test-time reasoning parameters for performance or latency without increasing the risk of LLM agents making policy-prohibited API calls.
